Task: Determine the minimum diameter of a solid circular shaft from a specified angle-of-twist limit under pure torsion.
Geometry: Solid circular cross-section of diameter d, uniform along its length.
Loading: A single applied torque T = 1,000,000 N·mm acting about the shaft axis. No transverse shear force, no bending moment, no axial load.
Length of the loaded section: L = 1500 mm.
Design constraint: Maximum allowable angle of twist φ_max = 0.75° (convert to radians for calculation: φ_max = 0.75 × π / 180).
Material shear modulus: G = 25939.8 MPa (N/mm²).
Assumptions: Small-deformation, linear-elastic behavior; homogeneous, isotropic material; uniform circular cross-section; pure Saint-Venant torsion; no stress concentration; no combined loading; shaft is fixed at one end with the torque applied at the other end.
Governing relation: φ = T L / (J G), where J is the polar moment of inertia of the solid circular cross-section.
Cross-section property: J = π d⁴ / 32.
Design equation: Set φ equal to φ_max and solve for d, yielding d = [32 T L / (π φ_max G)]^(1/4).
Units: All quantities are expressed in a consistent N-mm system (T in N·mm, L in mm, G in N/mm², d and J in mm and mm⁴ respectively, φ in radians).
Deliverable: The minimum required shaft diameter d_min (in mm), rounded up to a practical engineering value. Present the governing equation, substitute the numerical values, show the intermediate result for J, and state the final diameter.
Additional note: State that no factor of safety has been applied beyond the explicit twist limit; the result is the bare theoretical minimum.
